summary: Everyone prepares for judgment in their own language, and Carrie chooses not to interfere when Bjorn puts on armor.
panelPlan: Wide. Carrie sorts a thin file into order. Gunnar puts a library book into a bag after being told he cannot read during the hearing. The two male Kin dress carefully in their established clothing with small modern adaptations. Astrid ties or secures her usual outer layer, composed.
Insert. Bjorn lifts his armor from where it has been stored, maintained but not fetishized.
Medium: Bjorn fastens the armor over his clothing; his waist is clear and his hands are empty, leaving the armor itself as the formal statement.
Medium: Carrie sees him from across the room. She starts to speak.
Close on Carrie choosing not to. She instead checks his hands/waist visually for weapons.

Medium on Bjorn in armor: He stands fully dressed but unarmed while Carrie visually checks his empty belt and hands; Gunnar lifts his library bag into the edge of the exchange, turning the security check into ordinary household preparation.

dialogueInline.text: Gunnar, book stays in the bag once we go in.
I was going to ask about the armor.

directionInline.text: Exactly five displaced applicants are present: Bjorn, Gunnar, Astrid and the two established male Kin. Carrie is the caseworker. Bjorn's armor contains no weapons.

summary: Hearing-center security treats Bjorn's armor as an ordinary screening problem, not as a spectacle or threat.
panelPlan: Wide. Ordinary metal detector, trays, tired security staff, people removing belts and emptying pockets. Bjorn in armor stands in line with everyone else.
Medium. A security officer looks at the metal detector, then at Bjorn.
Insert: Bjorn places rings and other loose metal pieces into a gray security tray, then presents empty hands for the screening.

Two-shot at the security checkpoint: The officer runs the handheld wand along Bjorn's armor while calmly defining what is acceptable; Bjorn stands still with his rings and loose metal already in the gray tray, treating the ruling as practical procedure.
Medium: Officer waves him through after wanding. Bjorn accepts the ruling because it is clear.

dialogueInline.text: Mostly is a bad word in security.
No blades. No loose spikes. Nothing you can take off and swing.
He likes rules when they make sense.

summary: In the waiting area, Astrid quietly demonstrates one small piece of independence before anyone thinks to test her.
panelPlan: Wide. Plastic chairs, municipal notices, vending machine, families and individuals waiting for unrelated matters. The household sits together but not rigidly.
Medium on Carrie in the waiting room: She opens the thin file on her lap and starts offering one last rehearsal while the household sits loosely across ordinary plastic chairs.
Medium on Bjorn: Already dressed for judgment, he leans forward to ask who goes first; Carrie has to admit the folder contains preparation, not control over the room.
Medium: Astrid notices a posted NO FOOD OR DRINK BEYOND THIS POINT instruction, reads enough of it to understand, and calmly finishes/sets aside her coffee before Carrie mentions it.
Medium: Carrie notices Astrid's action, then returns to the file without commenting. Gunnar also notices.

dialogueInline.text: We can go through questions once.
You brought a folder and don't know?
It's a hearing, not a dinner reservation.

summary: The clerk calls the matter and immediately breaks the household's instinct to present itself as one unit.
panelPlan: Waiting-room doorway — Medium: A clerk calls the DTI temporal-residency docket and looks down the row of applicants as all five recognize their matter.
Wide. Bjorn, Gunnar, Astrid, and both male Kin rise together. Carrie rises with them.
Medium: Inside chamber. The clerk gestures to separate chairs / positions for identity verification.
Medium: Bjorn starts to remain standing beside the others; Carrie lightly touches the back of his assigned chair rather than physically steering him.
Wide from authority's viewpoint. Five displaced applicants now occupy five distinct seats, with Carrie at caseworker table nearby.

dialogueInline.text: DTI temporal-residency matter. All applicants, please.
You were standing next to it.

directionInline.text: Seat the five displaced applicants as five distinct people. Carrie remains at the separate caseworker position.

summary: The Hearing Officer identifies the real legal defect: the emergency intake file still treats Bjorn as the household's responsible adult and the other four adults as derivative members, a structure that cannot simply convert into five individual permanent statuses.
panelPlan: Wide: The Hearing Officer reviews the intake cover sheet and the later provisional-residence records while the five applicants sit together at one table.
Insert: Close on an old DTI intake field: HOUSEHOLD RESPONSIBLE ADULT — BJORN. Four associated adult members are listed beneath the master household record.
Medium on Carrie: Carrie recognizes the old classification immediately.
Medium on Hearing Officer: The Hearing Officer turns to the governing problem without accusation.
Reaction strip: Bjorn reads the significance before the others do. Gunnar looks at Carrie. Astrid remains still.

dialogueInline.text: Emergency intake has one responsible adult and four derivative members.
Permanent status is individual. I can't turn one household record into five grants.
So that box is the problem.
I'm going to assume there's history there.

summary: The Hearing Officer explains the stakes fairly: the defect can be cured in the hearing if the record now supports five independent adult applicants; otherwise permanent status must wait and the provisional case returns for reclassification.
settingText: Same Status Reconciliation Review hearing chamber.
panelPlan: Medium on Carrie: Carrie leans forward, ready to argue from everything that has changed since intake.
Medium on Hearing Officer: The Hearing Officer stops the argument only to define the legal lane.
Wide: The officer gestures to the five applicants rather than to Carrie's file.
Medium on Carrie: Carrie absorbs that her own recommendation cannot cure the record by itself.
Medium on Hearing Officer: The officer states the alternative outcome without menace.

dialogueInline.text: That hasn't been true for months.
I didn't say it was. I said I need a finding.
If the record supports five independent adults, I can correct it here.
They stay provisional. File goes back for reclassification. No permanent orders today.

summary: The first male Kin describes a life built from specific neighborhood obligations rather than abstract claims of belonging.
settingText: hearing chamber, first male Kin in individual questioning position.
panelPlan: Medium. The first male Kin sits forward, uneasy with formal questioning but not helpless.
Medium on First Male Kin: He answers by counting ordinary places from memory—laundry, bodega, building, park—without looking toward Carrie or Bjorn for confirmation.
Medium on Hearing Officer: The officer looks up from the notes and asks why those places matter, inviting explanation rather than testing recall.
Medium: First male Kin, a little confused by the need to explain ordinary repetition.
Wide: Reaction wide. Carrie hides a small smile; Bjorn takes the answer seriously.

dialogueInline.text: Where do you go without Ms. Carrie?
Laundry. Bodega. Building. Park if it's nice.
Things need doing. People notice if you say you'll come back and don't.

summary: The second male Kin proves that functional integration does not require pretending to know a permanent future.
panelPlan: Medium on Second Male Kin in the individual chair: He sits slightly angled toward the room, transit card tucked in one hand, listening carefully as the officer asks whether he is staying in New York.
Medium: He answers 'I'm staying' with present-tense certainty while keeping his posture relaxed, making no larger promise than the words themselves.

Two-shot with Hearing Officer: The officer waits after asking how long; Second Male Kin looks briefly toward the city-facing side of the room before admitting he does not know and clarifying that he never said forever.
Medium on Hearing Officer: The officer answers the actual legal concern plainly, separating permanent status from a promise to remain in New York forever.
Medium on Second Male Kin: Relief is small but visible as the distinction lands; he confirms he understands without turning the moment into a declaration.

dialogueInline.text: Are you staying in New York?
Permanent status does not require permanent residence.

summary: Bjorn begins to defend the second man's answer, catches himself, and lets another adult's incomplete statement stand on its own.
panelPlan: Reaction on Bjorn, visibly dissatisfied that the answer might be misunderstood.
Medium on Bjorn: He leans forward on instinct as though to translate or strengthen the other man's answer, one hand lifting from the table before the sentence is complete.
Close. He stops himself before Carrie or the Hearing Officer intervenes.
Medium on Bjorn: He lowers the hand and settles back into his chair, correcting himself aloud and leaving the other man's words untouched.
Medium: Hearing Officer makes a note and moves on without rewarding the moment. The second male Kin glances at Bjorn once; that is enough.

summary: Gunnar describes the parts of New York he has chosen for himself—books, familiar places, food, people and wandering—without turning independence into a navigation demonstration.
panelPlan: Medium on Gunnar in the individual questioning chair: He sits comfortably rather than at attention, answering that he goes places alone while his library bag rests by one foot.
Medium on Hearing Officer: The officer asks where Gunnar chooses to go, emphasizing choice rather than competence while keeping the notes secondary.
Medium on Gunnar: He names library, coffee, park, and aimless walking as ordinary preferences, glancing briefly toward the room as he thinks of each one.
Two-shot: The officer asks why; Gunnar gives the honest 'depends' with a small shrug, comfortable leaving the first answer incomplete.
Medium on Gunnar after a beat: He fills in the answer with books, food, weather, and sometimes simply wanting out of the apartment, revealing a life made of preferences rather than proof.
Medium: Hearing Officer. Gunnar considers the word rather than solving it.

dialogueInline.text: You go places on your own?
Where do you choose to go?
Library. Coffee. Park. Sometimes I just walk.
Books. Food. Weather. Not being in the apartment.

summary: During recess, Carrie sees that the hard problem is partly her own old intake decision; Silas offers to help, but the only useful thing is leaving the room to the people whose status is actually being decided.
settingText: Municipal hearing-center recess hallway outside the chamber.
panelPlan: Medium: Carrie stands with the old intake cover sheet open to BJORN — HOUSEHOLD RESPONSIBLE ADULT. Gunnar and Bjorn are nearby but not crowding her.
Close on Carrie: Carrie looks at the checkbox she made during emergency intake.
Medium on Silas: Silas appears with his overprepared binder held against his chest.
Two-shot Carrie/Silas: Carrie closes the old intake sheet.
Wide: Silas sits down with the binder unopened. Carrie turns back toward the hearing-room door instead of toward a new strategy.

dialogueInline.text: I had five adults, no IDs that made sense, no address, three languages in the room, and one pen.
Bjorn could answer. I used his name.
I have statements, photos, neighbor stuff—

summary: A mixed neighborhood record shows that belonging includes friction, correction, and continued contact rather than universal praise.
panelPlan: Insert on the case file: Brief complaint summaries record the early rooftop/property incident, smoke or noise friction, hallway problems, and the later corrected conditions.
Medium on Hearing Officer: The officer looks up from the complaint summaries and states that complaints exist without accusation, one hand holding the page open.
Medium on Carrie: She leans forward automatically to explain the early incidents, then stops as the officer continues reading the corrections already documented.
Medium: Hearing Officer raises one finger, reading further.

Wide across the hearing table: The applicants remain together while the officer frames conflict and repair as evidence of ordinary coexistence; Bjorn answers from the group without anyone rallying behind him.

dialogueInline.text: I see the corrections. I also see the same neighbors still there afterward.
I don't need perfect neighbors. I need people who can keep living beside each other after a problem.
They complained because we were wrong.
You don't hear that a lot in here, do you?

summary: Astrid is called after the louder applicants and immediately establishes that she will answer for herself rather than through Carrie.
panelPlan: Medium: Astrid moves to the individual questioning position without special framing.
Medium on Hearing Officer: The Hearing Officer checks whether Astrid wants caseworker assistance.
Medium on Carrie: Carrie turns slightly toward Astrid but does not speak.

Medium on Astrid in the individual chair: She answers the offer of Carrie's help directly, then looks once toward Carrie before adding that she does not need it; Carrie receives the correction without embarrassment.
Wide: Carrie sits back. The Hearing Officer continues without treating the answer as remarkable.

dialogueInline.text: Want Ms. Carrie to help if you get stuck?

directionInline.text: Underplay Astrid's turn. No hero framing, applause, or sudden transformation.

summary: One compact line of questioning reveals Astrid's practical independence: she can get home, buy what the household needs, and has neighborhood relationships Carrie did not catalogue as hers.
settingText: Hearing chamber with two restrained reader-facing ordinary-life cutaways.
panelPlan: hearing chamber — Medium on Hearing Officer: The officer asks one practical question tied to the independent-adult classification.
hearing chamber — Medium on Astrid: Astrid answers in concrete landmarks rather than transit jargon.
reader-facing prior ordinary life — Small cutaway: Astrid alone steps off a bus near the familiar blue-doored church carrying groceries; she moves with practiced certainty.
hearing chamber — Medium on Hearing Officer and Astrid: The officer follows with ordinary household and neighborhood questions.

reader-facing prior ordinary life — Small cutaway: Astrid at the bodega counter exchanges a familiar nod with the owner while choosing soap and needles; the Upstairs Neighbor passes her in the building hall in a separate sliver of the panel.
hearing chamber — Reaction two-shot: Carrie looks at her generic neighborhood-contact notes. Gunnar realizes Astrid knows routes he never taught her.

dialogueInline.text: If you leave here alone, can you get home and run an errand on the way?
Train. If it stops, bus to the blue church. Fruit stand, laundromat, home.
Who knows you on that route?

directionInline.text: The two cutaways are reader-facing illustrations of ordinary accumulated life, not evidence projected in the hearing. Keep the reveal mundane.

summary: Astrid completes the proof without a montage: she can ask for clarification, manages an ordinary day by choice, and makes clear that mutual reliance inside the household is not legal dependency on Bjorn or Carrie.
panelPlan: Medium on Hearing Officer: The officer asks a bureaucratically phrased independence question.
Medium on Astrid: Astrid refuses the wording rather than the question.
Medium on Hearing Officer: The officer sets aside the bureaucratic phrasing, relaxes the question into plain speech, and asks Astrid whether she runs her own day.
Medium on Astrid: Astrid answers with the ordinary shape of her day and no effort to impress the room.
Two-shot Astrid/Bjorn: The officer asks the question that matters to the old household classification.
Wide: Bjorn hears Astrid define the relationship without insult; Carrie does not translate or soften it.

dialogueInline.text: Do you independently procure ordinary necessities and manage routine travel without household supervision?
Do you run your own day?
Yes. Shop. Laundry. Where I need. Sometimes where I want.
We help each other. Not the same.

summary: After Astrid's testimony, the Hearing Officer returns to the unresolved record defect: strong individual lives do not automatically erase an old legal classification.
settingText: Same hearing chamber, after Astrid returns to the applicant table.
panelPlan: Wide: Astrid returns to the applicant table. The Hearing Officer stacks the testimony notes beside the old master household record.
Medium on Hearing Officer: The officer acknowledges what the testimony has established.
Insert: The old field HOUSEHOLD RESPONSIBLE ADULT — BJORN remains visible on the intake record.
Medium on Carrie: Carrie understands the distinction between facts and the legal record.
Medium on Hearing Officer: The officer states the remaining finding she needs.

dialogueInline.text: The file still says one is responsible for four.
Was it intake shorthand, or is it still true?

summary: Carrie owns the original classification instead of defending her file, explaining why it was reasonable during emergency intake and why leaving it unchanged became inaccurate.
panelPlan: Medium on Carrie: Carrie keeps the old intake sheet open in front of her.
Medium on Hearing Officer: The officer asks whether the designation was factually true at intake.
Medium on Carrie: Carrie answers without blaming the software or pretending the choice was meaningless.
Medium on Carrie: She then states the part that costs her professionally.
Reaction wide: The applicants hear Carrie acknowledge that the case record lagged behind their lives.

dialogueInline.text: At intake I needed one name.
Five adults. No IDs the system understood. No address. Everybody exhausted.
Bjorn could answer. I used his.

summary: The Hearing Officer tests the old hierarchy directly by asking whether Bjorn can consent, decide, or speak for the other adults; each answer separates respect for Bjorn from legal dependence on him.
panelPlan: Medium on Hearing Officer: The officer addresses the four adults listed under Bjorn's old responsible-adult designation.
Reaction sequence: First Male Kin answers first, matter-of-fact.
Reaction sequence: Gunnar answers with the distinction he has learned to live by.
Reaction sequence: Second Male Kin answers without looking to Bjorn.
Reaction sequence on Astrid: After the three men give longer variations of the answer, Astrid meets the officer's eyes and gives the shortest possible refusal of Bjorn's legal authority: 'No.'
Medium on Bjorn: Bjorn listens to four refusals of legal dependence without treating any as disloyalty.

dialogueInline.text: Can Bjorn decide status or housing for you?

summary: The Hearing Officer gives Bjorn the decision at the center of his season arc: correcting the record means surrendering the only legal document that still names him as responsible for everyone else.
panelPlan: Medium on Hearing Officer: The officer turns the old intake sheet toward Bjorn.
Close on Bjorn: Bjorn looks at the responsible-adult field, then at the four people beside him.
Medium on Hearing Officer: The officer makes the consequence precise.
Reaction strip: Carrie does not rescue him. Gunnar, Astrid and the two male Kin wait.
Close on Bjorn: Bjorn gives up the formal role without asking what replaces it.
Insert: The Hearing Officer draws one clean line through the responsible-adult designation and initials the correction.

dialogueInline.text: Mr. Bjorn, the record gives you authority they say you don't have.
Here, they're the same box. If I strike it, you stop answering for them.

summary: With the legal hierarchy removed, the Hearing Officer asks what actually remains between the five applicants; the answer comes from their continued choices rather than from Bjorn defining the household for them.
panelPlan: Medium on Hearing Officer: The officer sets the corrected intake sheet beside five separate applicant pages.
Medium on First Male Kin: First Male Kin answers from present life.
Medium on Second Male Kin: Second Male Kin preserves his uncertainty.
Medium on Gunnar: Gunnar answers without turning the household into a rule.
Medium on Astrid: Astrid makes the practical point everyone else has been theorizing around.
Medium on Bjorn: Bjorn does not add a collective declaration.

dialogueInline.text: Without that legal tie, are you still a household?
And none of them wash the cups.
She is right about the cups.

summary: The Hearing Officer asks Bjorn what remains of leadership after the legal responsible-adult role is removed; his answer is deliberately smaller and less polished than the speech he once would have given.
panelPlan: Medium on Hearing Officer: The officer looks from the corrected record to Bjorn's armor.
Close on Bjorn: Bjorn considers the question without performing certainty.
Medium on Hearing Officer: The officer checks the practical meaning rather than inviting philosophy.
Two-shot Bjorn/Gunnar: Bjorn glances once toward Gunnar, then answers for himself.
Wide: The answer lands without applause or reaction montage.

dialogueInline.text: What are you to them then?

summary: Carrie gives the final professional testimony the corrected record actually needs: she supports five separate permanent findings and accepts that doing so ends intensive case supervision rather than proving one collective integration score.
panelPlan: Medium on Hearing Officer: The officer turns to Carrie with five separate applicant sheets now visible.
Medium on Carrie: Carrie looks once at the old master file, then closes it.
Medium on Hearing Officer: The officer makes the professional consequence explicit.
Close on Carrie: Carrie answers without hedging or converting the applicants into one score.
Wide: The Hearing Officer separates the five applicant pages physically from the old master file.

dialogueInline.text: Ms. Carrie, do you support permanent status for each applicant separately?
That ends intensive DTI supervision as a condition of residence. You're not certifying one household unit.
They don't need a babysitter. They need normal paperwork.
Then I have what I need.

summary: The Hearing Officer grants permanent temporal-resident status only after correcting the defective household classification and making five separate findings from the testimony heard in the room.
panelPlan: Wide: The Hearing Officer reviews five separate pages, the corrected intake sheet and the thin case file. The cadence is administrative, not triumphant.
Medium on Hearing Officer: The officer states the first finding.
Reaction strip: The five applicants absorb the word individually in different ways.
Medium on Hearing Officer: The officer states the housing and supervision consequence.

Two-shot Bjorn/Hearing Officer: Bjorn leans forward just enough to reduce the ruling to the practical question that matters—whether they stay. The officer answers yes, and Astrid's quiet 'Good' lands from beside him.
Wide: The officer closes the old master household file and keeps the five individual records open.

dialogueInline.text: The corrected record supports permanent temporal-resident status for each applicant.
The Bushwick placement can continue under ordinary tenancy and program rules. Intensive DTI supervision ends.
And none of you is responsible for another's future decisions under this order.

summary: Outside the hearing room, the household begins processing the earned ruling, but Astrid simply returns to the ordinary independent life the hearing finally made visible.
settingText: Municipal hearing-center hallway, exterior steps and city sidewalk.
panelPlan: hearing-center hallway — Wide: Carrie immediately starts explaining administrative next steps while the five applicants emerge together.
hearing-center hallway — Medium on Astrid: Astrid checks an ordinary clock or folded receipt, shoulders her small bag and starts toward the exit.
Hearing-center hallway — Medium on Gunnar: He notices Astrid has already shouldered her small bag and is moving toward the exit while Carrie is still explaining the administrative aftermath.
Hearing-center hallway — Medium on Astrid walking: She answers without slowing or turning back, already re-entering her ordinary independent day as the others remain behind.
hearing-center exterior steps — Wide: Astrid descends into ordinary pedestrian traffic alone. No one follows to manage her route.
City sidewalk — Final wide: Astrid merges into ordinary pedestrian traffic while the others remain higher on the hearing-center steps for one beat, watching her go.

dialogueInline.text: Okay. Order gets entered, housing gets a copy, DTI—
And the first thing you do is leave?
